subject: forestSpirit
pitch: A small forest spirit, part deer and part mossy stone. A body of grey river stone covered in soft green moss, slender wooden legs ending in little hooves, branching antlers sprouting tiny white flowers and leaves, a pale wooden mask-like face with two glowing green eyes, and a few fireflies circling its head.
reasoning:
I'm planning the scale and structure for a deer-like spirit figure using three.js, sketching proportions and starting with a noise-displaced, grey stone-textured body built from an icosahedron.

For the rest of the creature, I'm layering flattened mossy icosahedrons onto the body, tapered cylinder legs and hooves, a tapered neck, and a pale wooden mask-like head with a tapered snout and small glowing emissive green eyes, possibly paired with a subtle point light. I'm also designing recursive branching antlers out of bark-colored cylinders with tiny white flower buds and leaf details at the tips, plus scattering small glowing firefly spheres around the scene.

Still working out positions...

For the face I'm adding eye sockets, small emissive green eyes, and a tapered muzzle extending forward. The antlers use a recursive branching function with seeded randomness for natural-looking splits, with tiny flower and leaf details at the tips, plus moss patches scattered across the body and neck using flattened, noisy icosahedrons. The stone body itself gets displaced vertices for an irregular, weathered surface.

I'm using a deterministic sine/cosine-based displacement function keyed to vertex position so seams stay consistent across duplicated geometry, then adding orbiting firefly spheres with shared emissive material near the head, a small tail nub, and defining the stone and moss materials with appropriate roughness values.

Writing the build function...

I'll scatter small flowers and flattened leaf cones at branch tips and some mid-nodes for natural variation, then work out moss placement across the body's top surface, adjusting the stone body geometry's scale to get the right proportions.

Now I'm positioning the neck and head: a pale skull shape, a flattened mask-like front plate, and dark ellipsoid eye sockets, all scaled and placed to sit naturally atop the body and neck.

Continuing facial details, I add a tapered snout with a tiny nose, carved brow-line accents in darker wood, and small leaf-shaped side ears. Then I lay out the legs with knee joints and hoof cylinders at front and back positions, add a small tail cone, and start placing fireflies around the scene.

Scattering fireflies around the head in a ring, adding a soft green point light inside the head for eye glow, and writing a displacement function that perturbs an icosahedron's vertices with layered sine/cosine noise to give the body an organic, carved-stone bumpiness before recomputing normals for flat shading.
